summary: This bill amends the Federal Water Pollution Control Act to let the Steering Committee and EPA Administrator jointly select and periodically reassess a fiscal agent (replacing the New England Interstate Water Pollution Control Commission) to manage funding and administration for the Patrick Leahy Lake Champlain Basin Program, authorize the Great Lakes Fishery Commission to conduct fisheries and invasive species work in the Lake Champlain basin, and extend program funding through 2032.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends the Federal Water Pollution Control Act to enhance administration of the Patrick Leahy Lake Champlain Basin Program, adds new responsibilities for the Great Lakes Fishery Commission on Lake Champlain issues, and extends the program's authorization from 2027 to 2032. These changes maintain and slightly extend federal funding commitments for the program, representing a minor expansion of government spending on environmental management.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, or revenue collection.
The bill contains no provisions related to healthcare, insurance, or medical services.
The bill contains no provisions related to firearms or gun regulations.
The bill contains no provisions related to immigration, borders, or visas.
The bill contains no provisions related to abortion or reproductive rights.
The bill contains no provisions related to military or defense spending.

The bill directly amends the Federal Water Pollution Control Act to improve management of the Lake Champlain Basin Program, including fisheries research, aquatic invasive species prevention, sea lamprey control, and ecosystem restoration. It expands the scope of federal environmental work in the basin and extends program authorization, clearly advancing environmental protections.
The bill contains no provisions related to welfare programs, food assistance, or social safety net programs.
The bill contains no provisions related to schools, education funding, or school choice.
The bill contains no provisions related to drugs, decriminalization, or enforcement.
The bill contains no provisions related to criminal justice, sentencing, or policing.
The bill contains no provisions related to trade, tariffs, or globalization.

By extending the authorization of an existing environmental program through 2032 and adding administrative and programmatic elements, the bill implicitly supports continued deficit-financed spending rather than prioritizing debt reduction.
The bill contains no provisions related to LGBTQ+ rights or protections.
The bill contains no provisions related to foreign aid.
The bill contains no provisions related to voting, elections, or election integrity.
The bill contains no provisions related to technology regulation or data privacy.
The bill contains no provisions related to labor, unions, or worker protections.
The bill contains no provisions related to religious liberty or anti-discrimination laws.
